subject: organic-chemistry-1
question: Which term describes two compounds that share an identical molecular formula but differ in how their atoms are connected?
explanation:
Structural (constitutional) isomers have the same molecular formula but a different bonding sequence, which gives them different physical and chemical properties. Butane and 2-methylpropane are both C4H10, each with 2(4) + 2 = 10 hydrogens, yet they differ in branching and boiling point. Allotropes are different forms of a single element, polymers are long repeating covalent chains, and members of a homologous series differ by successive —CH2— units, so their formulas are not identical.

ELI-10: Same parts list, different assembly, different product. C4H10 can be built as one straight chain of four carbons or as a three-carbon chain with a methyl branch, and both use 2(4) + 2 = 10 hydrogens because both are saturated. Because shape controls how tightly molecules pack together, the straight chain boils near 0 degrees Celsius while the branched one boils about 10 degrees lower. Recognizing isomers matters clinically because drug molecules with the same formula but different connectivity can act very differently in the body.
